title: Radiative Spin Caloritronics
abstract: We predict the spin thermal Hall effect in nonreciprocal magneto-optical many-body systems, in which a longitudinal radiative heat current generates a transverse accumulation of the spin angular momentum carried by thermal photons. We show that this effect and the inverse spin thermal Hall effect constitute an Onsager-Casimir reciprocal pair, thereby establishing heat and photon spin as coupled transport channels in nonreciprocal photonic systems. The second law of thermodynamics imposes fundamental bounds on the spin-heat coupling, leading to a thermal-spin figure of merit that quantifies the efficiency of radiative spin-heat conversion. Our results establish a complete thermodynamic framework for photon spin caloritronics and lay the conceptual foundations for spin-controlled thermal radiation and nonreciprocal photonic thermal devices.
summary: The paper develops the theory of photon spin caloritronics by predicting the Spin Thermal Hall Effect (STHE) in magneto-optical nanostructures. It proves that STHE and its inverse counterpart form an Onsager-Casimir pair, establishing a complete thermodynamic framework for coupling heat flow to spin angular momentum transport. This work lays conceptual foundations for designing nonreciprocal photonic thermal devices.
main_problem: To establish a complete thermodynamic framework for photon spin caloritronics by investigating the relationship between the Spin Thermal Hall Effect (STHE) and its reciprocal counterpart, the Inverse Spin Thermal Hall Effect (ISTHE).
main_result: The STHE and ISTHE form an Onsager-Casimir reciprocal pair, establishing a unified thermodynamic framework for photon spin caloritronics. The analysis yields a thermal-spin figure of merit quantifying conversion efficiency.
method: Linear response theory is employed alongside fluctuational electrodynamics to derive reciprocity relations between coupled heat and spin fluxes driven by temperature gradients.
model_or_system: The study models nonreciprocal magneto-optical many-body systems, specifically using four identical InSb nanoparticles arranged in a square lattice immersed in a thermal bath.
key_observables: Spin contrast ($\Delta S_z$), the thermal spin Hall susceptibility ($\chi_{	ext{STHE}}$), and the dimensionless figure of merit ($Z_{TS}$).
important_parameters: External magnetic field strength ($H_{	ext{ext}}$), temperature bias ($\Delta T$), and nanoparticle size/arrangement.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on linear-response theory and the application of Onsager–Casimir reciprocity relations derived from microscopic reversibility.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic relationship between heat gradients and spin accumulation (STHE) versus spin gradients and heat flux (ISTHE). Plots show $\Delta S_z$ dependence on $\Delta T$ and $H_{	ext{ext}}$, and spectral decomposition highlighting resonance features.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by defining coupled fluxes, applying linear response theory to derive transport coefficients ($G_{ij}$), establishing the Onsager-Casimir symmetry between STHE and ISTHE, and finally quantifying efficiency using a thermal-spin figure of merit.
why_interesting: This work bridges concepts from non-equilibrium thermodynamics (heat/spin coupling) with quantum optics and condensed matter transport, providing a theoretical framework for novel energy conversion devices based on spin polarization in photonic systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic of the: (a) radiative Spin Thermal Hall Effect where a temperature gradient ∆T and therfefore a heat flux JQ through a non-reciprocal network of C4 symmetry made with magneto-optical nanoparticles under the action of an external magnetic field Hext in the the z direction induces a variation ∆Sz of spin angular momentum in the transversal direction of primary gradient ; (b) Inverse Spin Thermal Hall Effect where a variation ∆Sz in one direction (due to a spatial variation of ecternal field), and therefore a spin current JS in the same direction, gives rise to a temperture gradient ∆T in the transverse direction even without temperature gradient (i.e. T1 = T2 = T).

FIG. 2. Thermal spin accumulation in the four-particle network of InSb nanoparticles as a function of (a) the longitudinal temperature difference ∆T for different external magnetic fields applied along the +z direction; (b) the external magnetic field magnitude Hext for different temperature differences; and (c) the external magnetic field magnitude Hext for temperature differences of opposite sign. The optical response of the InSb nanoparticles is described by the gyrotropic Drude–Lorentz model [23].

FIG. 3. Spatial distribution of the normal component Sz of spin angular momentum density in the plane z = 0 around the same C4 network of InSb particles when (a) ∆T = 100K and (b) ∆T = −100K under the action of an external magnetic field applied along +z of magnitude of Hext = 1T.

FIG. 4. (a) Thermal spin accumulation coefficient GST as a function of the external magnetic field Hext applied along the z axis for different equilibrium temperatures T0. (b) Spectral thermal spin accumulation coefficient GST (ω) at T0 = 300 K for Hext = 1 T and Hext = 5 T. The inset shows a magnified view of the spectral region where the hybridization of resonant modes occurs.
